Effect

A live effect of an item, see item.effects: it derives what is drawn from the item without changing the item itself, as the effects in Illustrator do. The effects of an item run in order, each on what the one before it returned. Each type of effect is a subclass with its params as properties, registered by its type, see Effect.types. Effects of types that aren’t registered keep their params and leave what they get as it is, so that they still round-trip. Effect.extend(src) creates new types.

Constructors

Effect([object])

Creates an effect of the type of its class, or of the type that the object names, see Effect.create(object).

    Parameters:

  • object: Object — the params of the effect, and its visible flag — optional

    Returns:

  • Effect

Example:

var path = new Path.Circle({
    center: [50, 50],
    radius: 20,
    fillColor: 'red'
});
path.addEffect(new Effect.types.offset({ distance: 10 }));

Properties

type

The type of the effect, which names its class in Effect.types.

Read only.

    Type:

  • String
visible

Whether the effect applies. Effects that aren’t visible are skipped.

    Default:

  • true

    Type:

  • Boolean
params

The params of the effect as a plain object. Each type of effect also has them as properties. Changing the returned object isn’t tracked.

Read only.

    Type:

  • Object
item

The item that the effect is part of.

Read only.

    Type:

  • Item⟋null
index

The index of the effect in the item.effects of its item.

Read only.

    Type:

  • Number⟋null

Static Properties

Effect.types

The classes of the effects by their types. Hosts can register their own classes for types here, to replace the ones of Paper.js.

    Type:

  • Object

Methods

clone()

    Returns:

  • Effect — a copy of the effect, without an item
remove()

Removes the effect from its item.

    Returns:

  • Boolean — true if the effect was removed, false otherwise
apply(art)

Applies the effect to the art that it gets: the item, or what the effect before it returned, which it doesn’t change. Subclasses override it, effects of unknown types return the art as it is.

    Parameters:

  • art: Item — the item to apply the effect to

    Returns:

  • Item — the result
equals(effect)

Checks whether the effect is equal to the supplied one.

    Parameters:

  • effect: Effect

    Returns:

  • Boolean — true if they are equal, false otherwise

Static Methods

Effect.create(object)

Returns the effect, or creates one from an object that describes it, { type, …params, visible }, of the class registered for its type, or of Effect for unknown types.

    Parameters:

  • object: Effect⟋Object

    Returns:

  • Effect
Effect.extend(src)

Creates a type of effect: a subclass of Effect with its type, which registers it in Effect.types, the defaults of its params, which become its properties, and its apply(art). The params of subclasses add to those of their base classes.

    Parameters:

  • src: Object — the definition of the type

    Returns:

  • Function — the class

Example:

Effect.extend({
    type: 'shrink',
    defaults: { amount: 0.5 },
    apply: function(art) {
        return art.scale(this.amount);
    }
});
path.addEffect({ type: 'shrink', amount: 0.8 });
